pr_title: Fix ActiveStorage duplicating blobs when replace_on_assign_to_many flag disabled
pr_body:
Fixes #40827

In this scenario, Active Storage assigned blobs in two different
ways. First, using the association setter method and next using
Active Storage `attach`. When `replace_on_assign_to_many` was
disabled, the un-persisted blobs was attached alongs with
attachable array consisting old and new blob.

This PR attempts to fix the issue by excluding the un-persisted
blobs while trying above mentioned scenario.

cc/ @santib @zzak

issue_context.title: Activestorage duplicating blobs when .attach is called
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Initialize an activerecord object that has say `has_many_attached :files` relationship. Ensure to set the files attribute with a ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile object.
2. Then call `.attach` on `files` with an activestorage blob object.

### Expected behavior
I should have two blobs waiting to be attached/persisted. One from each step.

### Actual behavior
I have 3 blobs waiting to be attached. 

From looking at the code, it seems `.attach` appends any existing blobs to the new attachables and then it calls the `files` setter method which itself appends any existing blobs to the "new attachables" from `.attach` . See code references below.

https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/95d4c50eb5d35c036a1a52fc66c81d11a84ddd37/activestorage/lib/active_storage/attached/many.rb#L35
https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/95d4c50eb5d35c036a1a52fc66c81d11a84ddd37/activestorage/lib/active_storage/attached/model.rb#L149

As a side note, if you use the setter method directly on step 2 to set the activestorage blob, then you get 2 blobs waiting to be attached. The issue only occurs when `.attach` is used. You could also just replace step 1 with a .attach call. You get the same results.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 6.1.0.rc2

**Ruby version**: 2.7.1

Thanks for the hard work by the Rails team!

@muyiwaoyeniyi I had this problem too.

After spent some hours debugging, I'd realize that use "files" in has_many_attached association could be the critical point leading to this. And it was!

I've changed the association to `has_many_attached :attachments` and fixed all controller references and it's working fine now.

Maybe "files" is a reserved word? Not sure, but I'm still encouraged to investigating what is causing this problem in the lib and maybe submit a PR...

I had the same issue (Rails 6.1.3.2). I tried lucasfp13's suggestions but was still facing the same problem.

What worked for me was to call `.save` on the model after each call to `.attach`, then I would end up with the correct number of attachments.

@abhaynikam Thanks for clarifying and I appreciate the Rails team!

So I looked into this and I think that this is intended behavior.

The following test cases pass, and are correct to me:

```ruby
  test "attaches two files" do
    user = User.new(name: "Tina", highlights: [fixture_file_upload("image.gif")])
    user.highlights.attach create_blob(filename: "racecar.jpg")

    assert_equal 2, user.highlights.size
    assert_equal "image.gif", user.highlights.first.filename.to_s
    assert_equal "racecar.jpg", user.highlights.second.filename.to_s
  end

  test "should attach two files with association setter and attach helper method" do
    user = User.new(name: "Tina", highlights: [fixture_file_upload("image.gif")])
    user.highlights.attach fixture_file_upload("racecar.jpg")
    user.save

    user.reload
    assert_equal 2, user.highlights.count
    assert_equal "image.gif", user.highlights.first.filename.to_s
    assert_equal "racecar.jpg", user.highlights.second.filename.to_s
    assert ActiveStorage::Blob.service.exist?(user.highlights.first.key)
    assert ActiveStorage::Blob.service.exist?(user.highlights.second.key)
  end
```

From: [this comment](https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/40827#issuecomment-859687927) and abhaynikam/rails@dad69c5ea3 (without `append_on_assign`). Respectively.

The thing that I didn't expect, but kinda makes sense, is that assign (`association=`) will replace the existing attachments, with this test:

```ruby
  test "should attach three files with association setter method" do
    user = User.new(name: "Tina", highlights: [fixture_file_upload("image.gif")])
    user.highlights = [fixture_file_upload("racecar.jpg")]
    user.highlights = [fixture_file_upload("report.pdf")]

    user.save

    user.reload
    assert_equal 3, user.highlights.count
    assert_equal "image.gif", user.highlights.first.filename.to_s
    assert_equal "racecar.jpg", user.highlights.second.filename.to_s
    assert_equal "report.pdf", user.highlights.third.filename.to_s
    assert ActiveStorage::Blob.service.exist?(user.highlights.first.key)
    assert ActiveStorage::Blob.service.exist?(user.highlights.second.key)
    assert ActiveStorage::Blob.service.exist?(user.highlights.third.key)
  end

# Failure:
# ActiveStorage::ManyAttachedTest#test_should_attach_three_files_with_association_setter_method 
# Expected: 3
#   Actual: 1
```

Maybe this is also intentional, but I'm concerned that this leaves dangling blobs that should be deleted?

The next step is to probably verify that and make sure there is test coverage.

For example, I would expect this test to fail without the `only: ActiveStorage::PurgeJob`, but it doesn't:

```ruby
  test "successfully updating an existing record to replace existing, independent attachments" do
    @user.vlogs.attach create_blob(filename: "funky.mp4"), create_blob(filename: "town.mp4")

    assert_no_enqueued_jobs do #only: ActiveStorage::PurgeJob do

    assert_equal "wherever.mp4", @user.vlogs.second.filename.to_s

```

Regarding the dangling blobs: That's a good point 👍 we can work on a fix that removes any orphan blob, just keep in mind that there are some border cases where one blob can be attached to multiple objects.

review_comments: Can we make this method private?
We won't be able to change this to a private method 😊 .
maybe instead of introducing this method we can call `blobs.select(&:persisted?)` inline where necessary?
I think `:nodoc:` is sufficient to make it Private API (even with public visibility) for documentation purposes.
As @zzak says - if we've marked something as `:nodoc:` any use is at your own risk 😄

The following test

```ruby
  test "attaches two files using association setter and #attach" do
    append_on_assign do
      user = User.new(name: "Tina", highlights: [fixture_file_upload("image.gif")])
      user.highlights = [fixture_file_upload("racecar.jpg")]
      user.save

      user.reload
      assert_equal 2, user.highlights.count
      assert_equal "image.gif", user.highlights.first.filename.to_s
      assert_equal "racecar.jpg", user.highlights.second.filename.to_s
    end
  end
```

would pass before this PR and fail with this PR. It's not respecting the `append on assign` behavior while the record is dirty, thoughts?

You are right. This test cases does fail. I would expect it to attach both blobs. So far what I found was since we are using `association_name=` setter methods which directly takes attachables as argument. It replaces with new attachables passed as argument whereas when used with `attach` sends attachable argument considering `(change&.attachables || blobs) + attachables.flatten`

Will dig deeper but somewhere I feel like if you use `association_name=` when record is dirty it shouldn't append. WDYT?

Yeah, I don't have a strong opinion.. It's hard to tell how it should work since the setter method appending attachments is weird by itself 😅 

I guess that if we can keep existing behavior it'd be better since it'd be easier for people to upgrade, if it's not possible then I guess I'd be fine introducing this change in behavior

@abhaynikam the behaviour with `replace_on_assign_to_many = false` is intentionally for backwards compatibility (see #36716). Give this PR changes that behaviour I don't think we can merge it as is and I'd rather see that setting deprecated in Rails 7.0 because as you can see it produces confusing behaviour (that's also George's intention from the original PR).
@pixeltrix I have updated the PR without breaking the backward compatibility. Could you please have another look at the PR? Tested it locally on master branch as well. cc/ @zzak @santib

@abhaynikam does this restore the behaviour to what it was in 5.2 or is it different? If it's fixing a regression from 5.2 then it's okay. Might be easiest to create the same test cases using two standalone examples - one using 5.2 and one using your changes.

What I'm saying is that de-duplicating things may actually be breaking backwards compatibility. An app may be assuming that behaviour and doing its own hack to fix it and we may break their fix. That's not necessarily a reason not to fix it but we should know what behaviour we're changing so that we're fully informed.

I'm suggesting we create two examples using the [bug report][1] template, one with 5.2 and one with your branch so that we can compare the differences.

[1]: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/main/guides/bug_report_templates/active_storage_gem.rb
